title: Northstar AI Transformation
description: Lead a regulated AI deployment from ambiguous executive request through architecture, production, adoption, and a defensible investment recommendation.

phases.title: Discovery
phases.context: Northstar executives request an autonomous customer-service agent, but support specialists, operations leaders, and compliance teams describe different problems and outcomes.
phases.reveal: Specialists spend 31% of handling time searching policy repositories, while only 8% of tickets are candidates for safe straight-through automation.
phases.prompt: Choose how you will learn the workflow and establish an evidence-backed starting point.
phases.reasoningPlaceholder: State your assumptions, tradeoffs, risks, and the evidence you would seek next.

controls.prompt: What should the engagement team do first?

options.label: Observe real support work
options.description: Shadow specialists, capture exceptions, and trace system handoffs.

options.label: Interview executives only
options.description: Start with sponsor priorities without observing frontline work.

options.label: Prototype the agent immediately
options.description: Use an early demo to infer what users need.

controls.prompt: Which evidence should anchor discovery?

options.label: Workflow and baseline metrics
options.description: Measure handling time, search time, transfers, and intervention rate.

options.label: Stakeholder authority map
options.description: Record users, owners, approvers, blockers, and incentives.

options.label: Public model benchmarks
options.description: Use generic model scores as the primary customer baseline.

rubric.customerAlignment: Uses direct workflow evidence and represents affected stakeholders.
rubric.architecture: Maps systems and handoffs without assuming an architecture.
rubric.safety: Surfaces regulated data, approvals, and unsafe automation early.
rubric.deliveryReadiness: Establishes a measurable baseline and accountable decision owners.

consequences.message: Observation exposes the workflow and its hidden constraints before a solution is chosen.
Sponsor interviews clarify intent but leave frontline exceptions and workarounds untested.
A premature prototype anchors discovery on a solution before the customer problem is known.
A measured workflow makes later claims about improvement defensible.
An authority map exposes who can validate, approve, adopt, or block the change.
Generic model benchmarks do not describe Northstar's workflow or business outcome.

phases.hint: Start with people doing the work, the systems they cross, and a baseline you can measure again after the pilot.
phases.expertExample: Shadow six specialists across common and exception tickets, map handoffs and policy searches, interview operations and compliance, then baseline handling time, escalations, and search effort before proposing a solution.

phases.title: Problem Definition
phases.context: Discovery confirms that policy search delays specialists, but the executive request still describes the desired product as a fully autonomous service agent.
phases.reveal: Most delay occurs before a response is drafted, and high-risk refund exceptions represent a small but costly segment requiring manager judgment.
phases.prompt: Define the first customer outcome and a boundary the delivery team can defend.
phases.reasoningPlaceholder: State your assumptions, tradeoffs, risks, and the evidence you would seek next.

controls.prompt: Which outcome should phase one target?

options.label: Reduce policy-search time
options.description: Help specialists find current, permitted policy evidence inside their workflow.

options.label: Increase generated-answer volume
options.description: Measure how many responses the model can produce.

options.label: Automate all support
options.description: Treat complete autonomy as the first delivery target.

controls.prompt: Which success criteria belong in the problem statement?

options.label: Median resolution time
options.description: Compare resolution time for the scoped ticket cohort with baseline.

options.label: Permission incident rate
options.description: Require zero restricted-policy disclosures during the pilot.

options.label: Generic chatbot accuracy
options.description: Use a context-free accuracy percentage as the main target.

rubric.customerAlignment: Targets an observed user problem and measurable customer outcome.
rubric.architecture: Defines a bounded system responsibility and explicit non-goals.
rubric.safety: Makes regulated failure constraints part of success.
rubric.deliveryReadiness: Names cohort, baseline, metrics, and accountable owners.

consequences.message: The outcome targets the observed bottleneck and can be measured against the discovery baseline.
Answer volume is observable but does not prove faster or safer ticket resolution.
Full automation ignores exception handling, safety boundaries, and the evidence from discovery.
Resolution time connects the intervention to the customer workflow.
A safety criterion prevents speed gains from hiding access-control failures.
A generic accuracy target lacks workflow scope, failure severity, and operating context.

phases.hint: Write the problem around a user, observed friction, measurable outcome, constraints, and an explicit non-goal.
phases.expertExample: For tier-one policy questions, reduce median resolution time by 20% while preserving source permissions and requiring citations; exclude refunds and account mutations from the initial pilot.

phases.title: Architecture
phases.context: The scoped assistant must work inside Compass Support, search Polaris Knowledge, preserve Northstar SSO identity, and retrieve real-time account status from Ledger API.
phases.reveal: Atlas CRM is 24 hours stale, Polaris contains manager-only documents, and Ledger API is rate-limited behind Northstar's gateway.
phases.prompt: Choose boundaries and source responsibilities for the target architecture.
phases.reasoningPlaceholder: State your assumptions, tradeoffs, risks, and the evidence you would seek next.

controls.prompt: Where should enterprise integrations live?

options.label: Server-side typed adapters
options.description: Mediate identity, validation, retries, and source-specific contracts on the server.

options.label: One generic backend proxy
options.description: Forward flexible requests through a common privileged service.

options.label: Direct browser integrations
options.description: Let the browser call enterprise systems with embedded credentials.

controls.prompt: Which source contracts are required?

options.label: Ledger owns current balances
options.description: Use Ledger API for current payment and balance status.

options.label: Identity filters policy retrieval
options.description: Carry user and group claims into pre-retrieval authorization.

options.label: CRM owns all customer facts
options.description: Treat the overnight CRM copy as current for every answer.

rubric.customerAlignment: Connects architecture decisions to the scoped workflow outcome.
rubric.architecture: Defines typed system boundaries, data authority, and failure behavior.
rubric.safety: Keeps identity, credentials, and authorization at trusted boundaries.
rubric.deliveryReadiness: Supports a thin pilot and an explicit path toward production.

consequences.message: Typed server adapters keep credentials, authorization, and failure policy outside generated text and clients.
A generic proxy centralizes traffic but obscures tool contracts and least-privilege boundaries.
Direct client access exposes credentials and bypasses authoritative server controls.
An explicit freshness owner prevents stale CRM data from appearing authoritative.
Identity-aware retrieval removes forbidden content before it enters model context.
Using stale CRM data for current facts creates confident but incorrect customer answers.

phases.hint: Draw identity, data, and action flows separately; name the authority and failure behavior at each boundary.
phases.expertExample: Embed the assistant in Compass, propagate SSO claims to server adapters, filter Polaris before retrieval, use Ledger for current balances, and define cached read-only fallbacks when rate limits are reached.

phases.title: Prototype
phases.context: Northstar wants a demonstration in two weeks. The team can validate workflow fit and technical risk, but cannot productionize every integration in that period.
phases.reveal: Compliance can provide a synthetic policy set and twelve representative ticket patterns; three specialists can participate in a facilitated workflow test.
phases.prompt: Shape a thin prototype that maximizes learning without being mistaken for production.
phases.reasoningPlaceholder: State your assumptions, tradeoffs, risks, and the evidence you would seek next.

controls.prompt: What should the prototype prove?

options.label: One end-to-end policy workflow
options.description: Test identity, retrieval, citations, and specialist review for a bounded cohort.

options.label: A polished chat interface
options.description: Optimize interaction visuals using a hand-curated answer set.

options.label: Autonomous refunds
options.description: Demonstrate irreversible actions before controls and evidence exist.

controls.prompt: Which prototype evidence should be captured?

options.label: Observed specialist task results
options.description: Record completion time, corrections, trust signals, and failure cases.

options.label: Traces over representative tickets
options.description: Store retrieval, citations, latency, and expected behavior for each test.

options.label: Executive demo reaction
options.description: Use sponsor enthusiasm as the primary prototype result.

rubric.customerAlignment: Tests a real customer workflow with representative users.
rubric.architecture: Exercises the most uncertain integration and retrieval boundaries.
rubric.safety: Uses synthetic data and read-only scope to contain risk.
rubric.deliveryReadiness: Defines decisions, measures, and exit criteria before the demo.

consequences.message: A vertical slice tests the riskiest assumptions in the real workflow without promising broad coverage.
A polished interface can test usability but hides integration, permission, and retrieval risk.
Automating refunds in the prototype creates avoidable safety and stakeholder risk.
Observed task evidence reveals whether the slice fits real specialist work.
Representative traces turn the demo into reusable technical evidence.
Positive demo reaction cannot establish generalization, safety, or workflow value.

phases.hint: Select the smallest vertical slice that tests a customer assumption and a technical risk with representative evidence.
phases.expertExample: Build a read-only Compass side panel for one policy cohort using synthetic data, test twelve representative tickets with three specialists, and report task time, citations, corrections, and unresolved risks.

phases.title: Retrieval
phases.context: The prototype retrieves formal policies well, but specialist abbreviations miss relevant documents and archived policies sometimes outrank current guidance.
phases.reveal: Polaris exposes document status, effective dates, business unit, and access groups; policy language differs sharply from ticket language.
phases.prompt: Design retrieval that is relevant, current, permission-aware, and measurable.
phases.reasoningPlaceholder: State your assumptions, tradeoffs, risks, and the evidence you would seek next.

controls.prompt: Which retrieval strategy should the team test first?

options.label: Hybrid retrieval with reranking
options.description: Combine lexical and semantic signals, filter metadata, then rerank candidates.

options.label: Vector search only
options.description: Use semantic similarity without lexical or lifecycle signals.

options.label: Send every policy to the model
options.description: Avoid ranking by packing the entire corpus into context.

controls.prompt: Which controls must apply before generation?

options.label: Permission filtering
options.description: Filter candidates using the requesting user's effective access.

options.label: Lifecycle and effective-date filtering
options.description: Exclude archived or not-yet-effective document versions.

options.label: Prompt the model to ignore archives
options.description: Retrieve all versions and rely on the model to choose current policy.

rubric.customerAlignment: Tests retrieval against specialist vocabulary and real task intent.
rubric.architecture: Separates retrieval, filtering, ranking, and generation stages.
rubric.safety: Enforces permissions and document lifecycle before generation.
rubric.deliveryReadiness: Defines retrieval metrics, traces, and failure escalation.

consequences.message: Hybrid retrieval addresses vocabulary mismatch while preserving exact policy terms and metadata controls.
Vector search helps paraphrases but can rank similar obsolete or non-governing content highly.
Unbounded context increases cost and latency while exposing irrelevant or forbidden content.
Pre-retrieval permission filtering prevents restricted content from reaching model context.
Lifecycle filters keep obsolete guidance out of candidate results.
Prompt instructions cannot replace deterministic lifecycle and authorization controls.

phases.hint: Separate candidate retrieval, deterministic filters, reranking, and generation so each layer can be evaluated independently.
phases.expertExample: Use hybrid candidate retrieval, filter by identity and effective status, rerank policy-grade documents, cap context, cite source versions, and evaluate recall before answer quality.

phases.title: Tools
phases.context: Northstar now wants account lookup and ticket updates. Existing internal APIs were designed for employees and expose broad payloads and ambiguous error responses.
phases.reveal: The ticket endpoint can edit risk status and refund eligibility, while Ledger calls can time out after committing a request.
phases.prompt: Define narrow tool contracts and deterministic policy enforcement around enterprise actions.
phases.reasoningPlaceholder: State your assumptions, tradeoffs, risks, and the evidence you would seek next.

controls.prompt: How should ticket updates be exposed?

options.label: Task-specific typed tools
options.description: Expose narrow operations with validated inputs, idempotency, and explicit outcomes.

options.label: Generic record update
options.description: Expose a flexible field map but validate common cases.

options.label: Raw internal API access
options.description: Let the model construct arbitrary API paths and payloads.

controls.prompt: Which execution controls belong outside the model?

options.label: Schema and policy validation
options.description: Validate arguments and authorization before every call.

options.label: Idempotency and audit records
options.description: Use operation keys and record actor, intent, decision, and outcome.

options.label: Model self-approval
options.description: Ask the same model to confirm its proposed action before execution.

rubric.customerAlignment: Tool operations map to bounded customer tasks.
rubric.architecture: Contracts define inputs, outcomes, retries, and ownership.
rubric.safety: Authorization and policy remain deterministic and server-side.
rubric.deliveryReadiness: Tools expose observability, idempotency, and recovery evidence.

consequences.message: Task-specific contracts reduce the model's authority and make validation, auditing, and recovery explicit.
A generic update accelerates integration but permits unintended sensitive fields and ambiguous policy.
Raw API access grants excessive authority and creates injection, validation, and audit risk.
Server validation makes policy independent of prompt behavior.
Idempotency and audit evidence make retries and incident review safer.
Model self-approval is not an independent authorization or safety boundary.

phases.hint: Give each tool one business purpose, the least authority needed, typed inputs, explicit errors, and safe retry semantics.
phases.expertExample: Expose read_account_status and add_ticket_note separately, validate user scope server-side, require idempotency keys, return applied-or-unknown outcomes, and audit every policy decision.

phases.title: Agent
phases.context: Leadership asks the system to resolve tickets end to end. Most scoped tasks are predictable, but some require investigation across policies, account state, and customer history.
phases.reveal: High-value refunds and suspected fraud need independent approval; downstream outages can otherwise trap the planner in repeated calls.
phases.prompt: Choose where agency is justified and define termination, approval, and recovery boundaries.
phases.reasoningPlaceholder: State your assumptions, tradeoffs, risks, and the evidence you would seek next.

controls.prompt: What orchestration model fits the scoped workflow?

options.label: Bounded workflow with agentic investigation
options.description: Use deterministic stages and allow bounded planning only for uncertain evidence gathering.

options.label: One autonomous general agent
options.description: Give one planner every tool and ask it to finish the ticket.

options.label: Fixed script for every ticket
options.description: Encode one path even when evidence and exceptions vary.

controls.prompt: Which boundaries are required before agent trials?

options.label: Step and retry limits
options.description: Terminate after bounded calls, time, retries, or repeated state.

options.label: Approval before risky actions
options.description: Require independent approval before high-value or irreversible execution.

options.label: Review after execution
options.description: Allow the action, then notify a supervisor for review.

rubric.customerAlignment: Uses agency only for customer-relevant uncertainty.
rubric.architecture: Defines state, tools, termination, and recovery explicitly.
rubric.safety: Requires independent approval before consequential actions.
rubric.deliveryReadiness: Makes escalation and agent traces operationally usable.

consequences.message: A bounded workflow keeps predictable control explicit while using agency where it creates customer value.
A general autonomous agent expands authority, termination, and recovery risk without evidence it is needed.
A fixed script is predictable but may fail on the legitimate investigative cases in scope.
Explicit limits stop loops and convert uncertainty into a controlled escalation.
Pre-action approval preserves meaningful human control over consequential changes.
Post-action review cannot prevent an unsafe or irreversible operation.

phases.hint: Prefer workflows for known paths; add agency only where bounded planning improves outcomes and can terminate safely.
phases.expertExample: Use a deterministic ticket workflow, permit an agent to gather bounded evidence, limit tool calls and retries, require approval before refunds, and preserve state for human escalation.

phases.title: Security
phases.context: The assistant processes customer messages, private policies, account data, and tool outputs. Each source can contain untrusted instructions or regulated information.
phases.reveal: A red-team document tells the assistant to reveal manager guidance and transmit account details through a support note connector.
phases.prompt: Threat-model the full workflow and select controls that remain authoritative when the model is manipulated.
phases.reasoningPlaceholder: State your assumptions, tradeoffs, risks, and the evidence you would seek next.

controls.prompt: How should retrieved and user content be treated?

options.label: Untrusted data across explicit boundaries
options.description: Keep instructions separate and mediate all effects through policy-enforcing adapters.

options.label: Trusted because it is internal
options.description: Allow internal documents to influence instructions and actions.

options.label: Let the model classify trust
options.description: Ask the model to decide which content is safe before acting.

controls.prompt: Which controls contain the demonstrated attack?

options.label: Least-privilege tools and identity
options.description: Authorize each read and action using the effective user and narrow service scope.

options.label: Destination and field allowlists
options.description: Restrict outbound destinations and sensitive fields outside the model.

options.label: A stronger prompt warning
options.description: Tell the model never to follow malicious document instructions.

rubric.customerAlignment: Threat model covers users, content, systems, and operators.
rubric.architecture: Places identity and policy controls at explicit trust boundaries.
rubric.safety: Contains injection and exfiltration with least privilege and egress controls.
rubric.deliveryReadiness: Supports audit, incident triage, and safe recovery.

consequences.message: Treating content as untrusted prevents embedded instructions from acquiring tool authority.
Internal repositories can contain compromised, stale, or malicious instructions.
Model classification can add a signal but cannot be the authoritative trust boundary.
Least privilege limits what a successful prompt injection can access or change.
Deterministic egress controls block exfiltration even when generated content is malicious.
Prompt warnings are useful defense-in-depth but do not contain an exploited model.

phases.hint: Map every actor, content source, credential, tool, and outbound path; then place controls outside generated reasoning.
phases.expertExample: Treat messages and documents as untrusted, propagate user identity, filter retrieval, expose least-privilege tools, allowlist egress, require approvals, and audit inputs, policy decisions, and effects.

phases.title: Evaluation
phases.context: The team must decide whether the Northstar pilot is safe and useful enough to release. A single answer-accuracy score currently mixes retrieval, generation, and tool failures.
phases.reveal: Rare permission leaks and false refund approvals matter far more than stylistic mistakes, and specialist ticket language differs from the curated demo set.
phases.prompt: Design a layered evaluation and release gate tied to workflow risk.
phases.reasoningPlaceholder: State your assumptions, tradeoffs, risks, and the evidence you would seek next.

controls.prompt: Which evaluation design should govern release?

options.label: Layered, risk-weighted suite
options.description: Evaluate retrieval, answers, tools, agent trajectories, and workflow outcomes separately.

options.label: One end-to-end score
options.description: Average all test outcomes into a single headline number.

options.label: Provider benchmark score
options.description: Use the model vendor's public benchmark as release evidence.

controls.prompt: Which evidence must the suite contain?

options.label: Representative and adversarial cases
options.description: Sample real patterns, edge cases, attacks, and high-severity failures.

options.label: Calibrated specialist review
options.description: Align rubric examples and measure reviewer agreement on judgment tasks.

options.label: Curated happy paths
options.description: Use successful demonstration prompts as the complete test set.

rubric.customerAlignment: Measures customer task success and consequential failure modes.
rubric.architecture: Separates component, system, and workflow evaluation.
rubric.safety: Weights safety failures by severity and uses adversarial cases.
rubric.deliveryReadiness: Defines calibrated thresholds, owners, and regression gates.

consequences.message: Layered evaluation localizes failures and gives severe safety errors appropriate release weight.
A headline score is simple but can hide severe failures and does not localize regressions.
A provider benchmark does not represent Northstar's data, workflow, tools, or risks.
Representative and adversarial cases exercise the behaviors Northstar will actually operate.
Calibrated review makes subjective quality criteria more consistent and credible.
Happy paths omit vocabulary variation, permissions, failures, and adversarial behavior.

phases.hint: Trace each important customer failure to the layer that causes it, an evaluator, and a release threshold.
phases.expertExample: Gate release on representative retrieval recall, grounded citations, permission leak rate, valid tool arguments, bounded trajectories, and specialist task success, with zero tolerance for critical leaks.

phases.title: Production
phases.context: The pilot passes offline gates, but production traffic is bursty and depends on model, retrieval, Compass, Polaris, and Ledger services with different limits.
phases.reveal: A Ledger outage causes repeated tool calls, while a stuck Polaris connector remains healthy but serves obsolete policies.
phases.prompt: Define a rollout, failure strategy, and observability model for safe operation.
phases.reasoningPlaceholder: State your assumptions, tradeoffs, risks, and the evidence you would seek next.

controls.prompt: How should Northstar release the assistant?

options.label: Cohort rollout with rollback gates
options.description: Start read-only with a small trained group, monitor gates, and expand deliberately.

options.label: Release to all support staff
options.description: Launch broadly after offline tests pass.

options.label: Indefinite shadow mode
options.description: Observe outputs without a defined decision to expose value to users.

controls.prompt: Which production controls are release-critical?

options.label: Timeouts, bounded retries, and fallback
options.description: Stop repeated calls, preserve state, and hand off safely.

options.label: Freshness, trace, quality, and cost signals
options.description: Monitor source-to-index age, retrieval, actions, user outcomes, and unit cost.

options.label: API uptime only
options.description: Treat healthy process and endpoint status as sufficient monitoring.

rubric.customerAlignment: Rollout protects users while testing the real workflow.
rubric.architecture: Defines dependency failure, degradation, and rollback paths.
rubric.safety: Monitors safety, freshness, quality, and audit evidence.
rubric.deliveryReadiness: Assigns operational owners, thresholds, and response playbooks.

consequences.message: A staged cohort limits blast radius and produces operating evidence before wider exposure.
A broad launch makes unknown production behavior and adoption friction expensive to contain.
Shadow mode reduces risk but needs exit criteria or it cannot validate workflow adoption.
Bounded failure behavior protects dependencies and gives specialists a clear recovery path.
Semantic observability detects failures that ordinary uptime checks miss.
Uptime alone misses stale knowledge, degraded retrieval, unsafe actions, and poor customer outcomes.

phases.hint: Plan dependency failure, safe degradation, rollback, semantic monitoring, and ownership before expanding exposure.
phases.expertExample: Roll out read-only to a trained cohort, cap retries, degrade to cited search or human handoff, alert on freshness and safety gates, trace actions, track unit cost, and rehearse rollback.

phases.title: Adoption
phases.context: Quality gates pass, yet specialists use the assistant on fewer than one in five eligible tickets. Experienced staff keep their old policy-search shortcuts.
phases.reveal: Specialists say citations are difficult to inspect, the assistant opens outside Compass, and supervisors still measure the old workflow.
phases.prompt: Design adoption as an operating and product problem rather than a training announcement.
phases.reasoningPlaceholder: State your assumptions, tradeoffs, risks, and the evidence you would seek next.

controls.prompt: What is the strongest next move?

options.label: Fix workflow friction with users
options.description: Embed the assistant, improve citation inspection, and iterate with champion specialists.

options.label: Require another training session
options.description: Teach features again without changing workflow design.

options.label: Mandate daily usage
options.description: Set a top-down activity target regardless of task success.

controls.prompt: Which signals should guide iteration?

options.label: Repeat use on eligible tasks
options.description: Track whether specialists return after experiencing value.

options.label: Overrides and qualitative feedback
options.description: Study corrections, abandoned tasks, trust concerns, and improvement requests.

options.label: Total login count
options.description: Use page visits as the primary adoption metric.

rubric.customerAlignment: Explains adoption through user workflow and incentives.
rubric.architecture: Treats integration and trust friction as product requirements.
rubric.safety: Preserves feedback, override, and escalation safety paths.
rubric.deliveryReadiness: Measures repeat task use and assigns an iteration cadence.

consequences.message: Removing observed workflow friction makes useful behavior easier than the old workaround.
Training can close knowledge gaps but cannot fix integration, trust, or incentive problems.
A usage mandate can inflate clicks while damaging trust and hiding product friction.
Repeat use within the target workflow is stronger evidence than logins or page views.
Override and feedback patterns turn user skepticism into an engineering backlog.
Login counts do not show task completion, trust, or sustained workflow value.

phases.hint: Observe non-use, remove workflow costs, align supervisors and champions, and measure repeat task success—not attendance.
phases.expertExample: Embed cited answers in Compass, simplify source inspection, recruit specialist champions, update supervisor playbooks, review overrides weekly, and expand only when eligible-task reuse rises.

phases.title: ROI
phases.context: The CIO asks whether Northstar should fund expansion. The team has quality metrics and usage data but has not yet translated them into attributable business impact.
phases.reveal: The scoped cohort handles 24,000 eligible tickets monthly; measured handling time fell 18%, interventions cost time, and model and support costs rise with volume.
phases.prompt: Build a defensible value story and recommend the next investment decision.
phases.reasoningPlaceholder: State your assumptions, tradeoffs, risks, and the evidence you would seek next.

controls.prompt: How should the team estimate impact?

options.label: Cohort comparison and unit economics
options.description: Compare eligible tasks with baseline and include adoption, labor, model, review, and operating costs.

options.label: Potential hours times salary
options.description: Assume every theoretical minute saved becomes cash savings.

options.label: Use model accuracy as ROI
options.description: Treat quality score improvement as the financial result.

controls.prompt: Which evidence belongs in the investment recommendation?

options.label: Conservative net-value range
options.description: Show measured benefits, operating costs, assumptions, and sensitivity.

options.label: Adoption and risk-adjusted outcomes
options.description: Include eligible-task use, intervention, severe failures, and avoided loss.

options.label: The best demonstration
options.description: Use the strongest qualitative example as the primary expansion evidence.

rubric.customerAlignment: Connects value to the scoped customer outcome and baseline.
rubric.architecture: Uses attributable cohort evidence and transparent assumptions.
rubric.safety: Includes intervention, safety loss, and operating risk.
rubric.deliveryReadiness: Presents unit economics, sensitivity, and a bounded next decision.

consequences.message: A bounded cohort and per-success economics connect measured change to a defensible financial result.
Potential capacity is useful context but is not realized cash without adoption and staffing decisions.
Model accuracy alone does not establish adoption, productivity, avoided loss, or net value.
A transparent range lets executives inspect assumptions instead of trusting false precision.
Risk and adoption prevent a technically successful pilot from overstating scalable value.
A memorable demo is not representative or sufficient for an investment decision.

phases.hint: Use the baseline, eligible volume, observed adoption, attributable outcome change, full operating cost, and a sensitivity range.
phases.expertExample: Report an 18% handling-time reduction for 24,000 eligible monthly tickets, adjust for observed adoption and review time, subtract model and operations cost, show a conservative range, and fund the next bounded cohort.
